original_test_intent: Measure five-minute Ethernet throughput over the designated ConnectX port with the SUT acting as server and a controlled peer as client, then verify bandwidth meets the project specification and both systems remain healthy.
original_method: Record SUT/peer NIC BDF/interface/port/MAC/IP/VLAN/MTU, driver/firmware, negotiated speed/FEC/autoneg, NUMA/CPU/power state and baseline counters/logs; obtain compatible approved iperf version and exact TCP/UDP/stream/window/port/direction profile; isolate the test path; start SUT server and confirm readiness; run peer client to explicit SUT IP for300 seconds with60-second intervals; capture full server/client output, CPU/temperature and before/after counters/logs; stop server, restore firewall/path and compare stable intervals/final throughput/error deltas to versioned thresholds.
manual_activity: Network owners designate ConnectX port, peer/path/isolation, iperf profile and thresholds; agent may orchestrate approved endpoints for one five-minute run and collect evidence.
required_inputs: SUT/peer hostname, NIC BDF/interface/port/MAC/IP, VLAN/MTU/route/firewall and production-isolation approval
ConnectX model/driver/firmware/link speed/FEC/autoneg plus NUMA/CPU affinity/power profile
Approved iperf v2 or iperf3 package/hash/version, TCP/UDP, direction, streams, window, port and roles
Five-minute window, CPU/thermal/network-impact abort limits and firewall/process cleanup
safety_requirements: Dedicated peer and production-safe test VLAN/path with explicit owner approval
Never infer interface/IP/server address or start both roles on one host unless that is a separately approved loopback case
Use authenticated access; verify server readiness and selected port/process ownership
Stop on wrong path/interface, production impact, loss/error storm, link flap, CPU/thermal limit or host instability
Cleanly stop only the test process, restore firewall/path and verify both endpoints; no automatic rerun

Stop test processes, compare counters/health and restore settings

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Unsafe and role-ambiguous: it runs both server and client from the DUT shell, uses insecure SSH and tails output. The source requires SUT server and a separate client, but omits the server IP.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: For approved iperf v2, start `iperf -s -i 60` bound to the SUT test IP/port, confirm readiness, then from the peer run `iperf -c <SUT_TEST_IP> -i 60 -t 300` with approved stream/window options; use distinct iperf3 syntax only if selected and preserve full logs from both.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: SUT server role, second-host client,60-second intervals,300-second duration, Common branch and15/15 minutes are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Run one topology-bound two-host test with complete endpoint/counter/CPU evidence and negotiated-link-specific acceptance.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact role/path/version/profile, interface binding, counters/retransmits, CPU/NUMA and cleanup.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A tail of client throughput cannot prove SUT server behavior, interval stability, link errors or post-stress workability.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Single-stream TCP may not saturate a high-speed ConnectX link; stream count and CPU/NUMA placement materially affect throughput and must match the approved spec profile.

project_override_considerations: The source syntax is iperf v2-like; do not silently substitute iperf3. The missing `-c` server address is an input gap, not permission to test loopback. Decide whether SPEC means line-rate utilization, application throughput, TCP or UDP, one or multiple streams and one or both directions.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Performance row14 Wistron-Performance Networking-00029-V004: approve exact SUT-server and peer-client ConnectX NIC/BDF/interface/IP/VLAN/MTU/port/path, driver/firmware/link speed/FEC/autoneg/NUMA/CPU profile and production isolation; select iperf v2 versus iperf3, TCP/UDP, direction, streams/window/port; provide300-second bandwidth/utilization, retransmit/loss/error-counter and host-health thresholds plus abort/cleanup policy.

review_improvement: Restores the source's two-host roles and turns a missing-address/tail-only sketch into an attributable link/path benchmark with complete endpoint and health evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: Throughput is a property of both endpoints and the intervening path, not just the SUT NIC. Tool version, TCP stream count, NUMA/CPU affinity, MTU and negotiated link/FEC can dominate results. Running client and server on the same host may measure loopback or an unintended route and cannot validate the ConnectX path. Per-interval stability and before/after counters are necessary to distinguish usable bandwidth from a run with retransmits, drops or link errors.
